full_judgment:
50. Facts giving rise to this appeal are that the appellants, herein, 8 (eight) in number, filed Case No. 649 of 1988 (Kha-1), House No. 5, Moghbazar (Outer Circular Road), New Number 70-71, Outer Circular Road, Moghbazar, Dhaka (herein-after referred to as the property in question) challenging the legality of enlisting the same in the `Kha' list of the abandoned buildings as abandoned property in the light of the provisions of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. LIV of 1985), shortly, the Ordinance and publishing the list so made in the Bangladesh Gazette dated April 28, 1986 stating, inter alia, that one Khan Mohammad Nuruddahar of village-Ratoil, PS-Kashiani, District-Gopalganj, purchased 18 decimals land of CS Plot No.327 and 22 decimals land of CS Plot No.328 appertaining to Khatian No.56 of Mouza-Bara Maghbazar, Police Station-Ramna, Dhaka. Said Khan Mohammad Nuruddahar sold the land as purchased by him to Zafar Tehrani on 23-6-1953. Zafar Tehrani again purchased the land of CS Plot No. 329 from Matilal Dey MajuMd.er in the name of his wife Amena Sultana as his benaMd.er on October 14, 1947. Zafar Tehrani also purchased the land of CS Plot Nos. 325, 326 and 332 in the name of his wife, Amena Sultana and daughters-Nargis Khanum and Rokeya Sultana as their benaMd.er from Fazle Ahmed Karim, Khan Bahadur Md. Solaiman, Sagiruddin Ahmed Surwardy and Fatema Fazal on 23-2-1960 and 9-3-1960. The land purchased by Zafar Tehrani was recorded in the SA Khatian in his name and in the names of his wife and daughters and while he was in possession and enjoyment of the said land, he gifted all the aforesaid purchased land to his son, Rafi Tehrani on 1-10-1971. Rafi Tehrani filed Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 to confirm the oral gift and obtained decree on 21-9-1972. Rafi Tehrani made an oral gift to his wife, Hosne Ara Begum on 3-9-1972. Hosne Ara Begum got possession of the property as gifted to her by Rafi Tehrani and got her name mutated in the revenue records. She filed Title Suit No.425 of 1978 to confirm the oral gift of her husband and obtained decree on 6-5-1980. She then transferred some land to appellant Nos.1-6 and 8 and the purchasers created municipal holding in respect of their respective portion of their purchased land. While Hosne Ara Begum and her transferees were in possession and enjoyment of the land, they noticed that their properties had been included in the `Kha' list prepared under the provision of the Ordinance and the said list was published in the Bangladesh Gazette. Thereupon, the appellants filed the case before the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka seeking exclusion of the property in question, from the list of abandoned buildings as published in the Bangladesh Gazette. 

 57. The case of the appellant was that one Mairan Bepari was the CS recorded tenant of the land in CS Plot Nos.325, 327, 328, 329 and 332 appertaining to CS Khatian Nos.189, 34, 131, 240, 128 and 127 of Mouza-Bara Maghbazar. Mairan Bepari became the owner of the properties of the aforesaid plots by inheritance as well as by purchase from the CS recorded tenants, Sagiruddin Sheikh and others. After the death of Mairan Bepari, the properties devolved upon his son, Abdur Rahman and others and after the death of Abdur Rahman, the property of the aforesaid CS plots devolved upon Abdus Sobhan (the appellant) and others and that by amicable arrangement with other co-sharers, Abdus Sobhan got the property of the CS plots as mentioned hereinbefore. Abdus Sobhan owned and possessed the property for more than 12(twelve) years before the promulgation of President's Order No.16 of 1972 (PO 16 of 1972). After the promulgation of PO 16 of 1972, the Sub-Divisional Officer, Dhaka on 21-7-1972 wanted to take over possession of the land and structures of holding Nos. 70 and 71, Outer Circular Road, Magbazar (hereinafter referred to as the property in question) by force and then the appellant along with another filed Title Suit No.183 of 1972 in the Court of the then Munsif, First Court (now the Assistant Judge) for permanent injunction against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar(South) Dhaka; the Secretary, Ministry of Works; the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, restraining them permanently from entering into the property in question, changing its character and from any way disturbing their peaceful possession therein. Subsequently, the suit being transferred to the Court of Munsif, Third Court, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No.926 of 1981. In the suit, on an application for temporary injunction to the above effect, an order of temporary injunction was passed in favour of the appellant on 8-5-1973. During the pendency of the suit, the appellant transferred .4148 acre land of CS Plot Nos. 326, 329 and 332 of Municipal holding No. 70 to Zakia Sultana and Lutful Sultana in June and July, 1973. Later on, in July, 1974, Zakia Sultana and Lutful Huda sold their shares to Anowarul Islam Beg and others. The appellant sold 3 kathas land from CS Plot Nos.328 and 329 on 28-1-1974 to Ayub Ali who transferred the same to Muttaqui Chowdhury and Murshida Akhter on 17-2-1975. The appellant thereafter made several sales to different persons from different plots mentioned hereinbefore. After the sale, how much remained, the appellant possessed the same and during the R.S. operation, Khatian Nos. 2562 and 2571 of Mouza-Bara Maghbazar were duly prepared in his name. The transferees from the appellant made permanent and semi permanent constructions as well as erected tin-shed and the said transferees got their names mutated in the revenue record and that they paid rents and that separate municipal holding numbers had been opened in their names. The appellant dealt with the property in question as of his and that he made transfers and there was no reason or occasion for treating the same as abandoned property. The property in question was never treated as abandoned property and that possession thereof was not taken over by the Government at any time nor any order or notice for surrendering the possession thereof was made or issued to him at any time and that no notice was served upon him or any person as per provision of section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance. That in a portion of the property in question (holding No.71), Parkul Tea Estate, was the tenant under the appellant and the same was taken over by Bangladesh Tea Board after promulgation of PO 16 of 1972 and thereupon the appellant came to know as to the enlisting of the property in question in the `Kha' list treating the same as abandoned property and then filed the aforementioned case before the First Court of Settlement, under section 7 of the Ordinance seeking exclusion of the same from the list of the abandoned buildings as enlisted in the gazette notification published as per provision of the Ordinance. The Court of Settlement rejected the case by its decision dated 28-12-1994. Thereupon, the appellant moved the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi in the aforementioned writ petition. 

 61. Of the two appeals, I shall deal with CA No.10 of 2003 first. At the risk of repetition, it is stated that the appellants sought exclusion of the property in question from the list of abandoned buildings on the fact that the same belonged to Khan Mohammad Nuruddahar of village-Ratoil, Police Station Kashiani, District-formerly Faridpur now Gopalganj being CS Plot Nos. 327 and 328 comprising an area of 0.18 acre land and 0.22 acre land respectively. The same was purchased by Zafar Tehrani by registered sale deed being Nos. 5173 and 5241 dated 23-6-1953. The land of CS Plot No.329 belonged to Motilal Dey MajuMd.er who sold the same in favour of Mrs. Amena Sultana, a benaMd.er of Zafar Tehrani on 14-10-1947 by a registered deed being No.5331 and the land of CS Plot Nos. 325, 326 and 332 belonged to Fazle Ahmed Karim, Khan Bahadur Md. Solaiman, Sagiruddin Ahmed Sarwardy and Fatema Fazle who sold the same in favour of Amena Sultana, wife of Zafar Tehrani and Nargis Khanam and Rokeya Sultana, the daughters of Zafar Tehrani by registered deed Nos. 3485 dated 23-2-1960, 3484 dated 23-2-1960 and 4208 dated 9-3-1960 respectively. The SA Khatian in respect of those plots of land was duly prepared in the names of the aforesaid purchasers. As a matter of fact, those properties were purchased by Zafar Tehrani in his own name and in the names of his wife and daughters. Zafar Tehrani made an oral gift of all the landed properties in favour of his only son-Rafi Tehrani. Rafi Tehrani having got possession possessed the same with exclusive title and got a decree in his favour in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 on 2-9-1972 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and thus his oral gift was confirmed. Rafi Tehrani married Hosne Ara Begum on 30-3-1970, he made an oral gift of the property in question to his wife-Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No.7) on 3-9-1972 who accepted the gift and took over physical possession of the property in question in presence of witnesses and the said oral gift was put in writing also. On 18-10-1972, Hosne Ara Begum filed Title Suit No. 425 of 1978 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka to confirm the oral gift made by her husband in her favour and obtained a decree on May 6, 1980. After that Hosne Ara Begum got her name mutated in the revenue record and that she transferred some land to appellant Nos. 1-6 and 8 and the purchasers got municipal holding number in respect of their respective portion of land. 

 69. From the impugned judgment and order, it further appears that respondent No.2, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, filed affidavit-in-opposition in Writ Petition Nos.968 of 1995, 975 of 1995 and 1398 of 1995. In Writ Petition No.975 of 1995, respondent No.2 categorically stated that as the original owner, Rafi Tehrani, had left the country before P.0.16 of 1972 came into being, the same automatically vested in the Government by operation of law. Neither the Government nor the other rival claimants in the property in question, namely, Abdus Sobhan, the appellant in CA No. 77 of 2003, did challenge that Rafi Tehrani was not the son of Zafar Tehrani. It is apparent from the decision of the Court of Settlement that the appellants in Civil Appeal No.10 of 2003 in support of their case that Zafar Tehrani (father of Rafi Tehrani) purchased 0.18 acre land and 0.22 acre land respectively of CS Plot Nos.327 and 328 from Khan Mohammad Nuruddahar of village-Ratoil, PS Kakhiani, formerly Faridpur, now Gopalganj by registered deeds being Nos. 5173 and 5241 dated 23-6-1953; that Zafar Tehrani purchased the land of CS Plot No. 329 from Motilal Dey MajuMd.er in the benami of his wife, Amena Sultana, by registered deed No. 5331 dated 14-10-1947 ad the land of CS Plot Nos. 325, 326 and 322 from Fazle Ahmed Karim, Khan Bandur Md. Solaiman, Sagiruddin Ahmed Sorwardi and Fatema Fazle in the benami of Amena Sultana, Nargis Khanam and Rokeya Sultana, his wife and daughters respectively by registered kabalas being deed Nos. 3485 dated 23-2-1960 and 3484 dated 23-2-1960 and 4208 dated 9-3-1960 respectively filed the documents before it. The Court of Settlement kept those documents outside their consideration on the ground that those "were not put and proved into evidence and marked exts", though it considered the other documents filed by the appellants, which were also not formally proved into evidence. Thus the Court of Settlement followed two different standards to consider the documents filed before it by the appellants. It is very significant to note that all these transferred deeds were executed and registered at a time when nobody thought of a law in the form of PO 16 of 1972 or the Ordinance and under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, these deeds have a presumption of correctness. Moreso, none challenged those deeds. It is also very pertinent to state that it was the specific case of the appellants that SA Khatians in respect of those plots were prepared in the name of Zafar Tehrani and the other purchasers and those were filed before the Court of Settlement as have been clearly mentioned in its decision. 

 District Dhaka, Police Station and Sub-Registrar Office Kaliakoir, Chasichala land appertaining to Dhaka Collectorate Touzi No.4827, Mouza Kawehakari 414, Khatian No.4/23 eastern portion of plot No.1948, are 1.65 decimals and of Touzi No. 27/5397/ 4827, Khatian No. 377/12 and 4/13, Plot No.1940, area 0.9 decimal being in total 1.74 decimal with one semi-pucca tin roofed house and bounded with pucca pillers and barbed wires." 

 81. In this regard, it is very pertinent and relevant to state that the property described in schedule-'C' to the plaint of Title Suit No.31 of 1972 was the property appertaining to Dhaka Collectorate Touzi No. 4827, Mouza Kawehakari 414, Khatian No.4/23, eastern portion of Plot No. 1948, area 1.65 acres and of Touzi Nos. 27/ 5397/ 4827 Khatian Nos.377/12 and 4/13, Plot No. 1940, area 0.9 acre total area being 1.74 acres with one semi-pucca tin roofed house and bounded with pucca pillars and barbed wires at Kaliakair was never enlisted as an abandoned property and Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No. 7) specifically asserted that she was in possession thereof. 

 82. The Court of Settlement doubted the acquisition of title by Rafi Tehrani and Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No.7) to the property in question on the observation that the khatians filed by firisti were the certified copies obtained on different dates after 1980 and that "If Rafi Tehrani and Hosne Ara got property getting delivery of possession, then they might produce original Khatians." In making the said observation, the Court of Settlement was totally oblivious of the fact that the Government did not at all challenge the ownership of Rafi Tehrani. Moreso, the Government did not at all challenge the genuineness or truthfulness of the khatians filed by the petitioners before it (the Court of Settlement). Further mere failure to file the originals of the khatians could not be ipsofacto disproved the acquisition of title of Rafi Tehrani in the property in question. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider that the Government did not at all challenge the fact that Rafi Tehrani was not the son of Zafar Tehrani and that in support of the case of the purchase of the property in question by Zafar Tehrani in his own name and in the name of his wife and daughters registered deeds were filed and in the context, it also failed to consider the legal inference and impact of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 where the title of Rafi Tehrani to the property in question along with two other properties, one being 21/1 Purana Paltan was declared. 

 99. It is true that in the depositions of Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No. 7) and Md.. Shahidul Haque Bhuiyan (purchaser from Hosne Ara Begum and appellant No. 1) who were examined in Case No. 649 of 1988 (giving rise to this appeal) they did not say about the payment of rents to the Government, payment of Municipal Tax and now City Corporation tax, payment of other bills for utility services, such as, electricity, gas, WASA, but before this Court, the documents have been filed showing that Hosne Ara Begum mutated her name with the revenue authority in respect of the property in question and she paid rents; papers have also been filed showing payment of rents by Md.. Shahidul Haque Bhuiyan (appellant No. 1), Mrs. Shikha Haque (appellant No.6), i.e. the purchasers from Hosne Ara Begum and the payment of bills for utility services, namely, electricity, gas and water supply. In the context, it may be stated that the documents have been also filed before this Court showing that Municipal holding was opened in the name of Zafar Tehrani and holding tax and other bills for utility services, such as, electricity, gas and WASA were paid in his name. The most important document produced by appellant No.1 and appellant No.6, i.e. the purchasers from Hosne Ara Begum is that the then Dhaka Improvement Authority (DIT) (now RAJUK) by its Memo dated 17-11-1982 gave them permission to construct a building in the property in question (the list of the abandoned buildings in which the property in question has been included was published in the official Gazette on 28-4-1986). The above mentioned purchasers obtained electricity supply line, took gas connection from Titas Gas Transmission and Company Limited and water supply line to their newly built houses. The approved plan has been also filed before this Court. It may be stated that in the writ petition, it was specifically stated that Hosne Ara Begum mutated her name and paid rents and those facts were not denied by the Government by filing any affidavit-in-opposition. The very fact that Hosne Ara Begum mutated her name with the revenue authority, paid rents prima facie showed that Hosne Ara Begum was in possession of the property in question when the Gazette notification was made under section 5 of the Ordinance. It is necessary to state that from the decision of the Court of Settlement, it is prima facie clear that the khatians in respect of the property in question were filed on behalf of the appellants of this appeal, but the Court of Settlement refused to consider those on the ground that the original khatians were not filed and that certified copies thereof were obtained on different dates after 1980. In the writ petition, it was also asserted that appellant No.1 (petitioner No. l in the writ petition) constructed a four-storied building and leased out the same to the National Bank of Bangladesh in 1989 and the said Bank is running a National Bank Public School and College and some of the correspondences between the Bank and appellant No.1 were annexed to the writ petition and they were marked as annexure-'C-C2', but the Government of Bangladesh, writ-respondent No.2 did not deny the said assertions by filing any affidavit-in-opposition 

 124. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider that the presumption attached to section 5 of the Ordinance is not sacrosanct and is rebuttable and in considering the presumption attached to section 5 of the Ordinance, it totally failed to consider the materials placed before it, particularly, the decree passed in Title Suit No.31 of 1972, the deposition of Rafi Tehrani in this suit, the order of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dhaka dropping the property of Purana Paltan of Rafi Tehrani from the list of abandoned buildings, the decree passed in Title Suit No.425 of 1978 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, the mutation khatian in the name of Hosne Ara Begum and the rent paid by her which prima facie proved that during the relevant period, i.e. 26-3-1971 to 28.021972, Rafi Tehrani was in possession of the property in question and subsequently he divested his ownership on Hosne Ara Begum, his wife, by oral gift and that she was in possession thereof. Therefore, the property in question did not answer the description of an abandoned property within the meaning of article 2(1) of PO 16 of 1972 and the presumption attached to section 5 of the Ordinance was very well rebutted. In the context, it is necessary to state that section 5 of the Ordinance does not say that to get a notice for surrendering or taking over possession as an abandoned property, one need be in possession of the entire property.
